subject.title: [Feature]: Add provider-profile routing policies for multi-account OAuth/API pools (starting with google-gemini-cli)

question: Should OpenClaw add a native opt-in provider-profile pool routing contract for batch/worker workloads, and what minimal public config/state surface should it expose first?
rationale: The remaining work changes public config, persisted auth/profile state, provider fallback semantics, status/probe output, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not invent those product boundaries or defaults.

options.title: Design Additive Core Pool Routing
options.body: Define a minimal opt-in provider/auth pool contract that keeps current session-sticky defaults and starts with one observable strategy before expanding to quota, bucket, and weighting semantics.

options.title: Keep This As Umbrella Tracker
options.body: Use this issue as the broad tracker while related issues keep narrower acceptance criteria for Gemini buckets, rotation depth, model-scoped auth defaults, and pace governance.

options.title: Defer To Plugin Or Sidecar Seams
options.body: Keep current core behavior and require a plugin/sidecar path until maintainers decide native pool routing is worth the new config and state surface.

recommendation.title: Design Additive Core Pool Routing
recommendation.body: Define a minimal opt-in provider/auth pool contract that keeps current session-sticky defaults and starts with one observable strategy before expanding to quota, bucket, and weighting semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision cuts across auth persistence, config compatibility, provider fallback policy, and public UX, and steipete has the strongest recent history across those surfaces.
